strings.title: THREE_WAY
strings.subtitle: Skill: joining three tables
strings.briefing:
An order only knows who bought it (customer_id) and what (product_id), as codes. The names live in two other tables: customers holds each person's name and city, and products holds each product's name and unit_price.

Build one table with a row for every order (all 60, none lost, none doubled) and these columns: order_id, customer_name, city, product_name, qty and line_total, where line_total is qty times the product's unit_price.

Two orders were placed by a customer the customers table does not list. Keep those orders; their customer_name and city simply stay empty.

In Python, df holds the orders, and customers and products hold the other two tables; put your answer in df (df = ...). That table is what gets judged.

In SQL, data holds the orders and customers and products the others. Create a NEW table named result that holds your answer: CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT ...; That table is what gets judged. You can run your query as often as you like; each run replaces the old result.
strings.task: Join orders to customers and to products so every one of the 60 orders appears once, with customer_name, city, product_name, qty and line_total (qty times unit_price).

starterCode.python:
# df = orders (60 rows). customers and products are the other two tables.
# Put your answer in df (columns: order_id, customer_name, city, product_name, qty, line_total).
df.head()

python: Two joins, one after the other: first orders with customers, then the result with products. Each join needs the key both sides share.
Use how='left' so an order whose customer is missing is kept. An inner join would silently drop those two orders.
df = df.merge(customers, on='customer_id', how='left').merge(products, on='product_id', how='left'); then df['line_total'] = df['qty'] * df['unit_price'] and keep the six columns.
sql: Join orders to customers, then to products, in one query: FROM data d LEFT JOIN customers c ON ... LEFT JOIN products p ON ...
LEFT JOIN keeps every order even when its customer is not listed. An inner JOIN would drop those two orders.

CREATE TABLE result AS SELECT d.order_id, c.customer_name, c.city, p.product_name, d.qty, d.qty * p.unit_price AS line_total FROM data d LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = d.customer_id LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = d.product_id;
